comparator.name: Global Responsibility and Leadership
comparator.sourceNotes: The current Groningen page confirms that the programme has been renamed Global Politics & Sustainability while retaining CROHO 59327. For the fixed Fall 2026 cohort, the 2026–2027 Ocasys catalogue still identifies the BSc as Global Responsibility and Leadership, and the official GRL curriculum brochure documents its three-major structure. The generic target does not select a major, so the first-listed major, Energy, Ecology & Climate, is instantiated by official order before considering UCR fit. The curriculum comprises 50 EC of named first-year foundations, 65 EC of genuine major-elective space, 15 EC of Personal Leadership Lab, Statistics II and Ethics and Global Responsibility, a 10-EC Living Lab, a 30-EC minor, and a 10-EC capstone thesis portfolio. These components account for 50 + 65 + 15 + 10 + 30 + 10 = 180 EC. Major-elective slots remain explicit rather than inventing course choices.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic GRL degree and does not specify one of its three formal majors. The official curriculum lists Energy, Ecology & Climate first, before Politics, Philosophy & Economics and Culture, Psychology & Global Health; it is therefore selected before and independently of UCR fit.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The first-listed Energy, Ecology & Climate major is the closest match. The two remaining formal majors—Politics, Philosophy & Economics and Culture, Psychology & Global Health—each generate a coherent, feasible and materially distinct UCR pathway. All direct interests are owned by the common core, and all three stable study directions are represented. The maximum of three alternatives is reached.

notes.text: Groningen embeds a formal 65-EC major, two leadership labs, an external-partner Living Lab, a 30-EC minor and a capstone thesis portfolio within one residential Liberal Arts and Sciences degree. UCR can assemble three rigorous 180-EC pathways around the same academic directions, but they are illustrative UCR curricula rather than Groningen majors and do not reproduce the Campus Fryslân Living Lab and portfolio structure.
